pull_request.title: Retry failed plugin worktree lookups instead of caching misses
pull_request.body:
Calling /wt-diff before git init caches a null worktree lookup for the session directory. Initializing the repository afterward does not help: subsequent commands reuse that miss and report no Git worktree for the rest of the module lifetime. A transient Git/process failure is similarly cached permanently.

Cache only successful locate results. Successful worktree lookups still avoid repeated Git subprocesses. This intentionally trades negative-cache savings for recovery: three repeated non-repository lookups now perform three Git probes rather than one. These probes occur when locating for the command/open pane; passive hooks still only note directories. Positive-cache invalidation behavior is unchanged.

Added a canonical Claude test for a failed command followed by a now-available repository, opening the pane and retaining the successful lookup cache. That canonical test is UNRUN: Claude Code plugin validate/test and the full UI integration gate are unavailable in this environment.

Local evidence is narrower: Node 24 executes the actual locate function body extracted from register.tsx, with TypeScript types stripped, against real temporary Git repositories. Four checks cover git init after a miss, a controlled transient process failure followed by actual Git discovery, successful-cache reuse, and repeated non-repository probe counts. Unchanged source: two failures/two passes. Fixed: four passes in 490ms. This does not execute the complete Claude module or establish hosted/full-plugin acceptance.

AI disclosure: implementation, tests and description were prepared with Codex and independently reviewed by another Codex agent. No human-authorship or human-review claim is made.
